statement: Can yoy update ordo, the echelon registry, and anything that needs to be updated?  We want to use all current echelon systems
approval.decision: OD-INDY-8 (kickoff release set: the newest stable, compatible, verified release of each Echelon system, approved in the Registry after Conditor qualification; if a component fails qualification, keep the newest compatible release and record the exception, VER-003), kemiller2002/indy-init docs/OWNER-DECISIONS-2026-10-24.md (indy-init#13). On 2026-11-02 the owner asked for Ordo, the Echelon Registry and anything else needing it to be updated so that all current Echelon systems are used, and, asked "Do you approve echelon-current 1.34.0, which moves Ordo from 1.19.0 to 1.20.0 (adds decision events) and Forma from 0.12.0 to 0.13.0 (long URLs, SHAs and paths now wrap inside containers; the npm package now ships its F# token validator), with everything else unchanged from 1.33.0? And may I record that approval for you?", answered "Yes, approve 1.34.0 and record it". The answer came before Conditor 0.10.19 was released; it is recorded only after REG-RU-007 passed against that release. Chat timestamps are approximate to the minute; the agent does not see exact message times
approval.recordedBy: anthropic/claude-code, on the owner's explicit approval and permission to record it ("Yes, approve 1.34.0 and record it"), after REG-RU-007 passed in CI against released Conditor 0.10.19 and Conditor qualified this exact set; no VER-003 exception applies

Replaced by Forma 0.13.0 (v0.13.0, 2fcd1073): LRP-001, Forma containers inherit overflow-wrap: break-word, so a long unbreakable token (URL, SHA, path) breaks inside its container instead of escaping it; the published tarball adds the F# token validator (tools/TokenValidator: Css.fs, Program.fs, Validation.fs, TokenValidator.fsproj; 582 files, 0.12.0's 578 plus these four) and package.json gains tokens:validate, with check and release:check now needing the .NET SDK. Superseded by the selected Arca 0.7.0, which carries its changes (via 0.6.0: the breaking opaque queue and receipt types of DF-ARCA-2026-0014, and the license change from MIT to PolyForm-Noncommercial-1.0.0 that the owner accepted). Known consumer incompatibility, not a VER-003 exception: Chrona declares arca 0.5.0 (conditor.json and Directory.Packages.props on Chrona main, 481e389) and its store code does not compile against 0.6.0 or later, so Chrona stays on 1.31.0 until it migrates

Replaced by Arca 0.7.0 (v0.7.0, 7e1f90d6), a minor release (DF-ARCA-2026-0015; arca#47, arca#48) for bounded queue-sync scheduling (ARCA-OFF-010). It adds Deferral (why an attempt stopped short, typed) with SyncAttempt, OfflineSync.attempt and OfflineSync.drive; RetryPolicy (a policy that could spin is refused); SyncSchedule (pure transitions with isDue and wakeAt); and SaveState.ofQueue. OfflineSync.step and run keep their results. Fixes: a GitHub 5xx read is ARCA.GITHUB.SERVER_ERROR, transient, and a 5xx to the ref update is an unknown outcome reconciled by idempotency key; ConnectivityChanged acts only on a change. Source-compatibility caveat: the public union CallFailure (Arca.GitHub) gains the case ServerError, so an exhaustive match on it in application code needs that case; otherwise 0.6.0 code compiles and behaves as before. The persisted queue format is unchanged and the license stays PolyForm-Noncommercial-1.0.0 (all three nuspecs). The three .nupkg files match checksums.txt and GitHub's API digests, and each verifies with gh attestation verify (release.yml on main at 7e1f90d6). Package dependencies are unchanged from 0.6.0: EchelonFoundry.Arca.Limen 0.7.0 needs EchelonFoundry.Limen.Store and .Contract >= 0.9.0 (limen-fsharp 0.9.0 selected), and Arca.GitHub needs Aegis.Core and Aegis.Integration.GitHub >= 1.0.0 (aegis 1.0.0 selected); EchelonFoundry.Fides.Arca 0.2.0 needs Arca.Core >= 0.1.0. Conditor has no Arca descriptor: released Conditor 0.10.18 accepts it as an unlisted nuget-library and installs the set's selection from its release-asset NuGet feed against the Registry's sha256 (REG-RU-007, conditor#123). Known consumer incompatibility, not a VER-003 exception: Chrona declares arca 0.5.0 and does not compile against 0.6.0 or later; it stays on 1.31.0 until it migrates, and Conditor 0.10.18's CI plans Chrona's 1.33.0 moves without applying them (conditor#123). No component failed qualification
